input: Apply for a professional certification in project management

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: There are many project management certifications (PMP, CAPM, PRINCE2, PMI-ACP, etc.) — the specific one determines all eligibility requirements, prep steps, and costs involved.
Certification costs range from under $100 to over $500+, plus study materials — knowing the budget determines which certifications are viable and which prep resources to use.
The user's current PM experience and education level directly affects eligibility (e.g., PMP requires thousands of hours of PM experience), so the starting point changes the plan entirely.
Some certifications require employer-verified experience hours, a PMI membership, or documented training hours — knowing what the user already has avoids redundant steps.
Whether the goal is just to submit the application or to also pass the exam determines how far the plan needs to extend and what counts as 'done'.
The user may prefer self-study, a boot camp, or an online course — this shapes the study plan and timeline significantly.
Whether an employer is sponsoring this or it is self-driven affects budget, urgency, paperwork requirements, and how experience hours get verified.

gold.taskTitle: Apply for a project management certification
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to pursue and apply for a professional certification in project management, covering everything from choosing the right cert to submitting the application.

questions.title: Which specific certification are you targeting?
questions.description: Identify the exact certification the user wants (e.g., PMP, CAPM, PRINCE2, PMI-ACP, CSM) so eligibility requirements and application steps can be tailored precisely.

questions.title: How many years of PM experience do you currently have?
questions.description: Establish the user's current project management background, since most certifications have minimum experience thresholds that must be met before applying.

questions.title: Is your employer sponsoring this, or are you self-funding?
questions.description: Determine whether this is company-driven or a personal initiative, as this affects budget availability, urgency, and whether experience documentation requires employer sign-off.

questions.title: What is your total budget for fees and study materials?
questions.description: Pin down the financial ceiling so the plan can recommend only viable certification paths, memberships, and prep resources within reach.

questions.title: Do you already have required training hours or a PMI membership?
questions.description: Find out which prerequisites the user has already fulfilled to avoid re-doing completed steps and focus only on what remains.

questions.title: How do you prefer to study — self-paced, course, or boot camp?
questions.description: Understand the user's preferred learning style so the prep plan recommends the right format of study materials and training programs.

questions.title: Does your goal end at submitting the application or passing the exam?
questions.description: Clarify where 'done' is for the user — application submission only, or the full journey through sitting and passing the certification exam.
